messages:
maria.k: RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight 'soft-migrate' path that borrows cold pages from other GPU pools instead of immediately evicting to host. Want feedback on safety and interface.
aj: Conceptually sounds good. What are the failure modes? e.g., donor suddenly needs pages back, or we accidentally starve its allocator.
maria.k: Failure modes: 1) donor demand surge -> we must be able to roll back or abort migrations quickly. 2) increased short-term peak memory on receiver while compaction finishes. 3) accidentally moving hot kv-cache lines.
sasha: For (1) we should return an opaque lease token from allocator on claim; runtime can `commit(lease)` or `release(lease)` and allocator can revoke with a fast callback if donor pressure rises.
devin_w: Lease token approach seems correct. Also include a soft-timeout on leases so long-running migrations don't hang. If revoked, receiver must either drop reference or trigger async writeback.
ben_p: How do we pick candidates? My idea: per-pool frag_index = weighted(run_length_score, free_fragment_ratio, recent_alloc_failures). Only pools with frag_index > threshold are eligible. Favor contiguous free ranges to avoid scattering.
aj: Agree. Add a hotness filter: any page with access_count_recent > H is ineligible. KV cache items get higher weight against stealing.
maria.k: Operational knobs: `soft_migrate.enabled`, `soft_migrate.max_bytes_epoch`, `soft_migrate.concurrent_tasks`, `soft_migrate.leash_timeout_ms`. Gate behind FF.
infra-bot: deploy-check: referenced keys: `soft_migrate.enabled`, `soft_migrate.max_bytes_epoch`, `soft_migrate.leash_timeout_ms`. Ensure defaults disabled.
sasha: Telemetry: emit per-pool `steal_attempts`, `steal_bytes`, `lease_revocations`, `donor_tail_latency_delta`. We need an alert if donor_tail_latency_delta > X for 5m.
devin_w: Performance cost: receiver will likely map new pages and keep old mappings until compaction frees donor holes. That temporarily increases memory pressure. Limit concurrent tasks and use slab-first policy: move smaller slabs first to cap peak.
ben_p: We should have a safety limiter: if cluster-wide free GPU memory < Y% then suspend soft-migrate. Also avoid cross-node unless NUMA penalty < Z.
aj: API shape for allocator runtime boundary: `claim_donor(pool_id, bytes) -> lease_id|string`, `try_commit(lease_id) -> success|retry`, `abort_lease(lease_id)` plus `on_revoke(lease_id) -> callback` for immediate fallback. Keep ops minimal.
maria.k: Nice. Also need contract doc: what states a lease can be in (claimed, active, committed, revoked, aborted). We'll include state machine in RFC.
sasha: Test matrix: synthetic fragmentation generator (create many small frees), background KV cache pressure, and simultaneous inference tails. Measure P99 latency, donor impact, and compaction time.
ben_p: Perf harness should capture histograms for donor/receiver latency and memory delta timeline. Add a canary rollout with very low steal_rate to detect regressions.
maria.k: One more thing: ensure host-pinned buffers and externally pinned CPU-backed tensors are excluded. Make exclusion whitelist by tag.
aj: Also consider backoff strategy: exponential backoff per-donor when revoke events happen.
maria.k: Action items: I'll draft RFC with state machine, config, telemetry, and perf plan. @aj please write frag_index formula. @sasha spec the exclusion/tagging rules. @devin_w prototype lease API. @ben_p set up dashboards/canary jobs.
ben_p: ack. I'll add dashboard placeholders and an alert recipe.
infra-bot: note: config keys must be added to deploy config before enabling feature.
maria.k: Thanks all. Filing RFC in a couple hours. :sparkles:
